shots.text: Domino's promised pizza in thirty minutes or free.
Then a courtroom made them pay seventy-eight million dollars.
Domino's was famous for speed. If your pizza was late, it was free. That promise built the brand.
Every order had a clock ticking on it, and every driver felt it.
In nineteen eighty-nine, a Domino's car and a woman's car collided in St. Louis.
She sued. She said the thirty-minute rush made drivers less safe.
Domino's said its drivers were never told to speed.
But in December of nineteen ninety-three, the jury awarded her over seventy-eight million dollars.
Days later, Domino's dropped the guarantee for good.
The boss said the promise had become a problem. Customers no longer saw it as safe. So it was replaced with a satisfaction guarantee.
The case was later settled for far less, and the amount was never made public.
A marketing promise that built the brand was ended by one court verdict.
